newsitem.title: USA: U.S DOE says Elk Hills crude output up to 33 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S DOE says Elk Hills crude output up to 33 pct.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Energy said Wednesday crude oil production from Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve here reached 33 percent of capacity, following a Monday brush fire that halted most output.
"It will probably be late Saturday or early Sunday before we're at full production," said DOE spokewoman Brenda Turner.
A brush fire of unknown origin raced into the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve late Monday and burned about half its 47,000 acres, DOE said in a statement.
The field is located in Kern County, which produces 60 percent of California's 560,000 bpd crude output.
The fire forced DOE to evacuate half its 600 employees and shut in much of its 60,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) production of light-gravity crude.
The DOE sells about 46,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of the crude to California refiners, with the remaining barrels taken by part-owner Chevron Corp.
DOE said the 18G zone of the field lost most of its 33,000 bpd production, while the less prolific 10G, or "shallow" zone lost less. 10G produces about 12,500 bpd.
On Tuesday, 18G production and shipments slipped sharply to 586 barrels, while shipments and production of 10G zone slipped to 8,000 barrels.
